newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns no company funds in private accounts.
newsitem.headline: China warns no company funds in private accounts.

text.p: China's central bank has warned commercial banks not to allow enterprises to put company funds into personal accounts, saying such practices led to tax evasion and corruption, the Financial News said on Thursday.

Although existing rules banned the use of personal savings accounts to hold company money, many firms had done so to give them easier access to cash and to avoid supervision of their funds, the newspaper said.
That often led to corruption and tax evasion, the newspaper said.
But commercial banks had turned a blind eye to the practice, hoping to attract more customers and boost their deposits, it said.
"These measures have increased risk on the banks, seriously played havoc with the financial order and ruined confidence in the banks," it said.

A notice issued by the People's Bank of China, the central bank, had called on commercial banks to stop processing such accounts and said it would step up supervision of the banks to ensure they were complying with regulations, it said.
Banks found violating the rules would be fined and any interest on money in such accounts would not be paid, it said.
